These load cell reports — role: test_report. Hmm, they are referenced as "the conformity was established by the results of tests and examinations provided in the associated OIML Test Reports". The indicator one NMi-16200818-01 is the type evaluation report for this certificate. The load cell ones are reference certificates/test reports. I'd set the indicator one to "type_evaluation_report" and the load cell ones to "test_report".

Components: The cert names load cells as components. Should I record them as components? Rule 6: "For complex instruments... record each as a components[] entry". Load cells used with indicator. The load cells are from different manufacturers: Tedea (1022, 1022P, LPS; 1242), Beijing True-Tec (PA06, PA06MG, PA06R; PA08R, PA08G, PA08L), Zemic (L6E3, L6D, L6D8). These are alternatives — any of these load cells may be used. I could record:

components:
- role: "indicator", type_designations: ["DP-4400"], manufacturer: not in schema but role... The schema for components is: role, type_designations[], alternatives, characteristics{}. I'll add:
  - {role: "indicator", type_designations: ["DP-4400"], alternatives: null, characteristics: {}}
  - {role: "load cell", type_designations: ["1022", "1022P", "LPS"], alternatives: "OR"}
  - {role: "load cell", type_designations: ["1242"], alternatives: "OR"}
  - {role: "load cell", type_designations: ["PA06", "PA06MG", "PA06R"], alternatives: "OR"}
  - {role: "load cell", type_designations: ["PA08R", "PA08G", "PA08L"], alternatives: "OR"}
  - {role: "load cell", type_designations: ["L6E3", "L6D", "L6D8"], alternatives: "OR"}

Each load cell group is an alternative to the others, and within each group the types are alternatives too. So alternatives "OR" within group. Actually the whole set of load cells is alternatives — all groups together are OR. Hmm, the schema allows alternatives within a component entry. I could put one component "load cell" with all type designations and alternatives: "OR". That seems cleaner:

- {role: "load cell", type_designations: ["1022", "1022P", "LPS", "1242", "PA06", "PA06MG", "PA06R", "PA08R", "PA08G", "PA08L", "L6E3", "L6D", "L6D8"], alternatives: "OR"}

But then manufacturer info is lost. The schema doesn't have manufacturer in components. I could add characteristics with manufacturer info... Actually the schema says components have role, type_designations, alternatives, characteristics{}. I could add a "manufacturer" key in characteristics? characteristics is for sub-characteristics. I think I'll keep separate entries per manufacturer to preserve info, and note alternatives: "OR" for types within each. Actually maybe I should keep the structure simple: one component entry per manufacturer group. That preserves the manufacturer association informally via... hmm, no field for it. I could add "manufacturer" as an extra key — the schema doesn't forbid extra keys but let me be conservative and include characteristics with manufacturer? Actually characteristics{} is a free object, so I can put {"manufacturer": "Tedea"} there? That seems like abuse but reasonable. Alternatively, I add an extra field "manufacturer" to each component. The instructions say don't fabricate but also structured extraction; adding a "manufacturer" key seems helpful and grounded in the text. I'll do that.

Also load cell compatibility: "For each model, the compatibility of load cells and indicator is established by the manufacturer by means of the compatibility of modules form, contained in OIML R76 edition 2006 Annex F." Could add to description or a note. Maybe in certificate description or certified_type.description. I'll include it as part of certified_type.description.

Characteristics table (page 3):
- Accuracy class: (III) or (IIII) → covered by recommendation.accuracy_classes. Could also be a type_level characteristic: accuracy_class value "(III) or (IIII)". I'll put it in recommendation.accuracy_classes: ["III", "IIII"]. Maybe also include as type_level characteristic? Redundant; I'll skip or include. I'll include in recommendation only.

- Maximum capacity: 100 kg ≤ Max ≤ 500 kg → value {min: 100, max: 500}, unit kg. Label: maximum_capacity.
- Verification scale interval: e ≥ 0,05 kg → value {min: 0.05, max: null}, unit kg. Label: verification_scale_interval. Note decimal comma → 0.05.
- Weighing ranges: Single interval / Multi-interval → value: "Single interval, Multi-interval"? It's a list of options. I could record as weighing_ranges with value ["Single interval", "Multi-interval"] — but value must be number | {min,max} | string. So string "Single interval or Multi-interval". Or use config_level with axis "weighing_range"? Hmm. It's two configurations: single-interval and multi-interval instruments. The next two rows differentiate:
  - Maximum number of scale intervals (one weighing range): n ≤ 3000 divisions
  - Maximum number of scale intervals (multi-interval): n ≤ 3000 divisions (per partial weighing range)
  
  These could be config_level entries with axis "weighing_range" with conditions "single_interval" and "multi_interval":
  - attribute: max_number_of_scale_intervals, axis: weighing_range, values: [{condition: "single interval", value: {min: null, max: 3000}, unit_symbol: "divisions"}, {condition: "multi-interval (per partial weighing range)", value: {min: null, max: 3000}, unit_symbol: "divisions"}]

  Also maximum_number_of_partial_weighing_ranges: 2 (dimensionless).
  
  And weighing_ranges: value "Single interval, Multi-interval" — I'll record as type_level: weighing_ranges: {value: "Single interval or Multi-interval", unit_symbol: null}.

- Temperature range: +5 °C / +35 °C → value {min: 5, max: 35}, unit_symbol: "°C".
- Power supply voltage: "AC/DC adapter 100 – 240 V AC 50/60 Hz, or internal battery pack 9 V DC"
  Per rule 3, split:
  - power_supply_voltage: For AC adapter: {min: 100, max: 240}, unit "V". But there's also battery 9 V DC. Hmm, two power supply options. Could use config_level with axis "power_supply": conditions "AC/DC adapter" → 100-240 V AC 50/60 Hz; "internal battery pack" → 9 V DC.
  
  Option: type_level:
  - power_supply_voltage: {value: {min: 100, max: 240}, unit_symbol: "V"} for the adapter
  - power_supply_frequency: {value: {min: 50, max: 60}, unit_symbol: "Hz"}
  - power_supply_type: {value: "AC/DC adapter"}
  - battery_voltage: {value: 9, unit_symbol: "V"} (DC)
  - battery_type: {value: "internal battery pack, DC"}
  
  Or config_level with axis "power_supply_option":
  - attribute: power_supply_voltage, axis: power_supply_option, values: [{condition: "AC/DC adapter", value: {min:100,max:240}, unit_symbol: "V"}, {condition: "internal battery pack (DC)", value: 9, unit_symbol: "V"}]
  - attribute: power_supply_frequency, axis: power_supply_option, values: [{condition: "AC/DC adapter", value: {min:50,max:60}, unit_symbol: "Hz"}]
  - attribute: power_supply_type, ... 

  I'll use config_level since it's a configuration choice. Rule 5 says use config_level when attributes vary by configuration. Yes, power supply is a configuration option.

  Actually, maybe simplest: type_level entries for the adapter (main) and battery separately. But config_level is more faithful. Let me do config_level:

  config_level:
  [
    {
      "attribute": "power_supply_voltage",
      "axis": "power_supply_option",
      "values": [
        {"condition": "AC/DC adapter", "value": {"min": 100, "max": 240}, "unit_symbol": "V"},
        {"condition": "internal battery pack", "value": 9, "unit_symbol": "V"}
      ]
    },
    {
      "attribute": "power_supply_type",
      "axis": "power_supply_option",
      "values": [
        {"condition": "AC/DC adapter", "value": "AC"},
        {"condition": "internal battery pack", "value": "DC"}
      ]
    },
    {
      "attribute": "power_supply_frequency",
      "axis": "power_supply_option",
      "values": [
        {"condition": "AC/DC adapter", "value": {"min": 50, "max": 60}, "unit_symbol": "Hz"}
      ]
    }
  ]

  Hmm, but the structured value shape in config values: "{condition, value, unit_symbol}". OK.

- Software identification: Version number: 1.xx (xx = 03…99) → software_identification: {value: "1.xx (xx = 03…99)"} — string value. Or software_version: value "1.xx", software_version_range... I'll do software_identification with string value "1.xx (xx = 03…99)". Hmm, maybe better: software_version: {value: "1.xx (xx = 03...99)"}. Keep as is.

- Maximum number of scale intervals: n ≤ 3000 divisions → in config_level as above. Unit "divisions" — dimensionless-ish; unit_symbol "divisions".

Type-level vs model-level: The characteristics are the same for all models (DP-4400 etc.) presumably; no per-model matrix given. So type_level for non-config attributes.

The cert covers multiple model variants: DP-4400, MS-2xxx, MS-3xxx, MS-4xxx, MS-5xxx, MS-6xxx, MS-7xxx, MBF-6xxx, MS21-NEOxx, MHS-2xxx. Since >1 model variant, include model_family with models[] entries. family_name: null (no explicit family name). Each model: model_id as given, label maybe same. x = 0…9 wildcard applies to the "xxx" parts. I'll note in label.
